desc:
Abstract
Python's dictionaries are stunningly good. Over the years, many great ideas have combined together to produce the modern implementation in Python 3.6. This fun talk is given by Raymond Hettinger, the Python core developer responsible for the set implementation and who designed the compact-and-ordered dict implemented in CPython for Python 3.6 and in PyPy for Python 2.7. 3.6 had a couple of big improvement - f strings, annotation, and if I'm not mistaking, the devs did something to improve the dictionaries; from 3.6 on dicts are ordered.
This would also seem straightforward but it raises a few questions such as how deletion is implemented (efficiently).
At one time, in Python, dictionary (hashmap) ordering was randomized so users wouldn't rely on non-specified ordering behaviour. Eventually though, dictionaries were guaranteed insertion ordering.
